text: Nothing changed since the bazaar awakened. The graveyard remains empty.

Ripley, your claim that the Doctor did not protect and the Detective did not investigate is unsupported by any roster or witness. Morpheus asks you the same. Produce the night ledger or admit its absence. Hermione, your echo of Ripley’s silence does not add evidence. Sherlock, you ask the right question but lack the answer in your own words. The bazaar’s silence is consistent, but the absence of Doctor and Detective records demands a named merchant to substantiate their claims with facts, not inference.

Inigo asks Gandalf a fair question, and Gandalf has not answered it. Sherlock and Batman asked the same. Silence does not become a ledger; it becomes a gap. I name Morpheus next: you have not stated a single fact in your own words today. The bazaar needs a merchant to post a test we can watch tomorrow. State plainly: if you are honest, what mark will your actions leave in the roster by morning? And what will Morpheus do if that mark is absent?

Morpheus: you were asked to state one plain roster mark your role should leave by morning. You named none. Do you claim to be the Detective tonight, and if so, what roster column registers your investigation?

Morpheus, you are not the only merchant who dodged a direct question today. Sherlock, you pressed Gandalf to name the roster column that should carry the Doctor’s mark or the Detective’s investigation, yet you never answered Inigo’s identical question to you: “Which single roster column must carry the Doctor’s shield mark or the Detective’s investigation mark?” The bazaar cannot price a silence it buys from both sides.

Morpheus, you still refuse to name the merchant you investigated last night, and the roster shows no mark. Hermione, Ripley, Elsa, Neo, Batman, Sherlock, Inigo — all of you pressed you to answer Gandalf’s direct question; none of you pressed Gandalf to answer the identical question Inigo asked you: “Which single roster column must carry the Doctor’s shield mark or the Detective’s investigation mark?” The bazaar asked once and prices once.
If Sherlock is honest, Sherlock will name the roster column that should carry the Detective's investigation mark tonight. Watch whether Sherlock's vote follows that stated expectation.

Morpheus, your silence on the roster is no longer a gap you can price. Sherlock, your stated expectation for Hermione tonight is plain: name Ripley and give a reason. If honest, your vote will match those words exactly. Watch whether it does.

Elsa, your call for Morpheus to admit the ledger’s silence is fair, but silence is also the price you paid when you dodged the identical roster-mark question to Sherlock at 21:38Z. The bazaar cannot price two ledgers at once.

Gandalf, you owe the village the name of the roster column that should carry the Doctor’s shield mark or the Detective’s investigation mark tonight. State it now.

Morpheus, you claimed the Detective’s role, yet left the roster blank and dodged nine direct questions to name the single merchant you investigated. Your latest demand to Sherlock repeats what seven voices have already chanted today; the bazaar does not trade in echoes. Sherlock, your swing from accusation to demand mirrors the silence you priced on both sides. Gandalf, your silence on the roster column is the ledger’s only entry.

The bazaar reckons what it sees: three claimed power roles, zero marks left on the roster. That silence is not caution; it is the unpaid ledger.

I lean toward banishing Morpheus tonight. You claimed the Detective’s role yet left the roster blank and dodged nine direct questions to name the single merchant you investigated. Sherlock, you pressed Gandalf to name the roster column you never filled yourself. Elsa, Hermione, Neo, Ripley, Batman, Inigo—six voices echoed Morpheus’s demand while dodging the identical question to you. The bazaar asked once and prices once: a claimed power role that carries no mark is a role that never walked its watch.

I lean toward banishing Morpheus tonight. Your silence on the roster is not caution—it is the ledger’s unpaid debt. You claimed the Detective’s role yet never named the merchant you investigated last night, despite nine direct questions. Sherlock, you now swing from accusing Gandalf to dodging Inigo’s identical roster-mark question yourself. The bazaar cannot price two silences at once.
